tasks.task: Map the current customer journey from real evidence

items.when: When you have reviews, tickets, comments and notes and need each stage and step mapped
When research notes exist but nobody has said whose journey this is
When you want a quick stage-by-stage draft with feelings and pain points to correct
When the map follows your departments, to redraw it around the customer's worries
When the map is tidy boxes and nobody has walked each step as a customer
Before the map is shared, to tie each pain point to a review, ticket or number

tasks.task: Analyse NPS results and find the reason behind a score change

items.when: When scores and comments are in and you need drivers, fixes and owners
When answers sit in a connected survey tool and you need themes and quotes for a period
When score comments must be read with tickets and calls to get one ranked signal
When the score fell, to rank likely causes from the before and after numbers
When leaders need a findings table with honest caveats on who answered
Before you report a score, to check how far the questions and sample can be trusted

tasks.task: Plan an NPS, satisfaction and effort survey programme

items.when: When you need the questions, the moments to ask and rules on who is asked how often
When the moment is just after an order and the business is an online store
When a one-off deeper survey is needed beside the regular score
Before launch, to get a bias review, a shorter question list and a pretest plan
When the plan chases delight and nobody measures how hard it is to get help

tasks.task: Follow up unhappy customers and log what was fixed

items.when: When customers scored you low and asked to be contacted
When one issue has been stuck for weeks and needs facts, an escalation and a reply
When each follow-up needs a reply in the right tone and notes on what to check first
When the first draft sounds cold or defensive, to see it in two other tones
Before sending, to check every promise in the reply is one you can keep

tasks.task: Build a touchpoint inventory and audit

items.when: Before mapping or redesign, or when customers get too many messages or mixed ones
When the list is built, to rank where the touchpoints disagree with each other
When you can share the site, emails, pack and ads, to score what each one says

tasks.task: Draw a service blueprint for one journey

items.when: When the path is mapped and you need the staff, systems and hand-offs behind each step
When you want each step listed with touchpoints, friction and the systems behind it
When customers wait at a hand-off, to find the one stage holding everything up

tasks.task: Rank journey fixes and write the future journey with owners

items.when: Each quarter, to move from scores and maps to a short list of fixes with owners
When the current map is agreed and the fixes need ranking by evidence and effort
When one page or flow loses people, to find where layout, defaults or order stop them
When budget allows one of two fix programmes, to see both with cost and dates
Before owners sign up, to name why the fix plan could fail

tasks.task: Write the quarterly customer experience report

items.when: At quarter end, to give leaders one honest page on how customers feel and why
When the report must follow the quarter's surveys, fixes and reviews in order
When the analysis is long and leaders need the answer first with the impact in numbers
Before it goes to leaders, to check each score and count against its source

tasks.task: Diagnose why customers delay, drop off or ignore a message

items.when: When customers do not act and you need the barrier named and a small honest change
When users sign up and drift away, to find the cause in the first steps and habits
When people keep getting one form or step wrong, to see what in the design misleads
When prospects stay with the old way, to rank the habits and worries holding them
When the fix is more reminders, to ask if the action is too hard or the prompt badly timed
When staff blame the customer for an error the design invites

tasks.task: Design small, honest nudges and a test plan

items.when: Before any nudge, to be sure which barrier it is meant to remove
When you need a set of messages, each with one small step and the best timing
When you want several honest changes to compare, each tied to a known mental model
When one change is picked and needs a hypothesis, sample size and reading plan
When the team is sure a nudge will work, to ask what past cases actually showed

tasks.task: Draft a reply to a formal complaint

items.when: When a formal complaint needs a clear, fair, complete reply for a person to approve
When the complaint asks for money back and the answer is yes, partial or no
When the customer is furious, to try a version that names the feeling first
Before approval, to check each promise, the tone and any admission in the draft

tasks.task: Check complaint deadlines and find root causes

items.when: When complaints need a daily, weekly and monthly routine with clear owners
When you hold a complaint log and need what is near its deadline and what keeps causing them
When several complaints look related, to find the shared pattern and a fix plan
When a cause is proposed, to test the chain of whys against the facts

tasks.task: Design a mystery shopping programme and scoring form

items.when: When a multi-site business needs fair scenarios, a weighted form and a shopper briefing
When there are no written standards to score against, to draft checkable ones first
When rivals should be shopped too, to plan buying from each and noting the follow-up

tasks.task: Report mystery shop results across sites with coaching notes

items.when: When scores are in and you need a fair comparison of sites and notes for each manager
When sites differ by a few points, to see if the gap is real or just a few visits
When the group owner needs one page across all sites with the answer first

tasks.task: Build a quality scorecard for calls, support or site visits

items.when: When you need weighted standards and a scoring form staff will see as fair
When each standard must be something a reviewer can check as done or not done
When you have a call recording and want notes and coaching on how it went

tasks.task: Check how a chatbot or AI agent tells customers it is AI

items.when: Before launch or at review of any AI that talks to customers by chat, email or voice
When you have recent bot chats, to find missed questions and wrong answers
When wrong answers are found, to propose fixes and cases to retest
When the bot serves EU customers, for a first read of the duties that apply

tasks.task: Write a retention and win-back plan

items.when: Before the plan, to see when each sign-up group stops coming back
When you have account data and need to know who is at risk now
When you know why people leave and need a cancel flow and save offers
When you have cancel reasons and need one honest save per reason with numbers to track
When lapsed buyers should be asked back, timed to how they really reorder

tasks.task: Write a customer guide, welcome pack or onboarding plan

items.when: When new customers need phased steps, milestones, owners and email templates
When the welcome is a 14-day run of emails and texts on how to use the product
Each week, to see where the new cohort stalls in its first 30 days
When the guide uses internal terms, to put it in words a new customer knows
Before it is sent, to read the pack as a new customer and list what they still must ask

tasks.task: Summarise the research on one customer behaviour

items.when: When you need sources chosen by clear rules and their findings pulled together
When every claim in the summary must carry a source or be marked unsourced
Before the summary is used to justify a change, to check each study says what you say

tasks.task: Build personas from research notes

items.when: When interviews, surveys or tickets are in and you need personas from the patterns
When each persona needs its own path and a test plan to go with it
Before delivery, to check each trait traces to evidence and none is invented

tasks.task: Build the weekly or monthly CX numbers report

items.when: When the report lists only scores, to find the inputs the team can control
When you know who reads it and what they decide, to pick metrics and a layout
When the same report must be rerun each period from the same sources
When two teams report different numbers for the same score, to reconcile the definitions

tasks.task: Write service standards and the procedure behind them

items.when: When the service feels different each time and needs one page of checkable standards
When staff need the steps, who does what and the edge cases written down
When the standards read like a script and leave staff no room to help

always.when: Before any map or report leaves, to tie each score, count and quote to a dated source
Before a report or customer letter is shared, to catch typos and one stage named two ways

helpers.when: When the map or diagnosis needs new interviews, a focus group or review mining first
When the fix is in the support queue, its targets, macros or staffing
When the stuck step is a screen, form or flow that needs redesign and a usability test
When score drivers need proper statistics or data joined from several systems
When the retention plan must become live email and message flows
When the AI check finds the bot itself needs rebuilding, not only its disclosure

gaps: No library item writes mystery shopping scenarios, a shopper briefing pack or a weighted scoring form
No library item compares scores across sites fairly and writes coaching notes for each site
No library item builds a touchpoint inventory across channels; the one workflow checks message consistency for stores
No library item sets survey programme rules: who is asked, at which moment and how often
No library item tracks close-the-loop cases from low score to fix and outcome
No library item checks a nudge for dark patterns or for harm to vulnerable customers
No library item runs a complaint log with deadlines set by a regulator or a code of practice
No library item checks how an AI chat or voice bot discloses that it is AI
No library item builds a quality scorecard for calls or support tickets with calibration between reviewers
No library item draws a service blueprint as a diagram with front-stage and back-stage lanes
No library item offers clearly different versions of a welcome pack or a complaint reply to compare
No library item applies a named behaviour model such as COM-B or EAST to a customer problem
